claims.text: Mechanical sliding continuously disrupts the passivating oxide film.
Disruption of the passive film exposes fresh alloy surface that corrodes more rapidly.
Localized corrosion degrades the surface microstructure.
Corrosion-induced surface degradation makes the alloy more susceptible to wear.
Wear and corrosion form a mutually reinforcing feedback loop under tribo-corrosion.
The feedback loop causes total degradation to exceed the sum of isolated wear and corrosion degradation.
The initial high-entropy alloy has an intact, naturally formed passive oxide layer.
The initial passive oxide layer provides corrosion protection.
The governing structural mediator is the passive oxide layer together with the relative rates of its mechanical removal and regeneration.
Repeated oxide removal lowers surface wear resistance through corrosion-mediated microstructural deterioration.
Tribo-corrosion will produce notably greater total degradation than the additive wear-only and corrosion-only baselines.
The wear contribution will be enhanced under combined tribo-corrosion relative to isolated wear.
The corrosion contribution will be enhanced under combined tribo-corrosion relative to isolated corrosion.
The proposed mechanism should operate when mechanical oxide removal outpaces oxide reformation.
Rapid oxide healing can suppress the proposed synergistic feedback.
The proposed mechanism may not dominate in alloys lacking a robust oxide layer.
The magnitude of synergistic degradation may vary substantially with alloy composition and environmental conditions.

contradictions.description: The wear-only test is specified to use an inert, non-corrosive medium while the combined test uses a corrosive medium, yet the conditions state that pH and electrolyte composition are held constant across tests. Those environmental properties generally cannot both remain constant while one medium is corrosive and the other is inert.
